title: LeetCode Spaced Repetition Tracker
oneLiner: An FSRS-6 review queue that schedules each problem for when you are about to forget it.
claim: Replaces brute-force repetition with a memory model, then paces the backlog so a first import does not become a wall.

metrics: Retrievability modelled as R(t) = exp(ln(0.9) * t / S) over stability and difficulty
Daily quota of 6 cards by default, adjustable to 4, 6, 8, 10 or 15
Cards sorted by mathematical urgency, lowest retrievability first
Imported problems start with raised stability, pushing first reviews 8 to 15 days out
Rich CSV imports bypass external lookups and insert in under a second

media.alt: The tracker dashboard showing the daily spaced-repetition review queue with a progress bar and due cards
media.caption: The daily review queue. Six cards, then the backlog rests.

proof.architecture: Submissions sync from LeetCode in the background on a fifteen-minute cooldown, or in one click through a bookmarklet that hands over solved history through a stateless JWT exchange. Grades of Again, Hard, Good and Easy update stability and difficulty, and the schedule is recalculated against the retention target.
